transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-19 15:00 UTC / Duration 45m / Attendees: Nina (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Marta (CSM), Samir (Vertex HoMLOps), Ava (Vertex Platform), Liam (Product), Jordan (Security)

[00:00] Nina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick check — 45 minutes on the calendar, main goal is to line up the cutover plan and next steps for the pilot rollout. Carlos will walk through the canary and monitoring details.
[00:18] Carlos: Cool, hi all. So recap: last week we finished the latency and quality tuning, quantization profile seems good for your 2k token median workload, throughput is within expected range. Today's stuff: canary strategy, A/B tradeoffs, slos, runbook, and the smoke test checklist.
[00:35] Samir: Great, yeah we've been running the test harness, and we pushed ~10k inferences through yesterday. Latency p95 was around 320ms for hosted variant, 260ms on Dedicated in our quick bench, but some variability when sequence lengths spike.
[00:50] Carlos: Right, that aligns with what we saw. Need to prime the KV cache for the warm paths — during canary we should pre-warm top prefixes, otherwise cold-starts will distort the canary metrics.
[01:05] Ava: When you say pre-warm, is that automated from Redwood side or we run a script?
[01:10] Carlos: We can provide a priming script — it's a small load generator post-deploy that sequences the common prompts. We'll include it in the runbook.
[01:18] Liam: Quick question on canary percentage: what do you typically recommend? 5%, 10%?
[01:24] Carlos: For this class of workload we usually start at 5% for 24 hours, then 20% for another 24 hours if metrics look stable — unless your traffic pattern or SLAs require faster ramp. For Vertex's customer-facing product, I'd propose 5 -> 25 -> 100 over 72 hours with manual gate at each step.
[01:41] Samir: Manual gates are fine. We want automatic rollback if error-rate jumps or latency exceeds SLO — what alerts do we need?
[01:47] Marta: We'll set threshold alerts in the Redwood Console. Typical guardrails: error-rate > 1.5x baseline, p95 latency > 1.8x baseline, model-quality regressions on a small eval set.
[01:58] Jordan: On the security side we need audit logs and KMS integration. Does Dedicated support customer-managed keys?
[02:05] Nina: Yes, Dedicated and Private both support KMS/HSM integrations. We'll attach the integration guide; you can do either Redwood-managed or bring-your-own via AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault.
[02:16] Jordan: Also retention for audit logs — we need 12 months immutable. Can you confirm?
[02:20] Nina: For Dedicated we can enable longer retention; I'll confirm exact SLA on immutability with infra team and add to the runbook.
[02:27] Carlos: Back to rollout: we should define explicit rollback criteria in the runbook — e.g., if p95 latency increases by >30% sustained for 15 minutes, or if user-level error rate >1% for 5 minutes, then traffic is shifted back to the previous model/version. We'll include run commands for immediate rollback via the control plane and an ops runbook page.
[02:50] Ava: For network cutover we need the VPC peering details and egress IPs. Also how do we handle canary traffic routing from our API gateway?
[02:59] Carlos: We'll provide a routing snippet — you can route a percentage via header-based routing or weighted upstreams in the gateway. For the VPC peering, we'll share the CIDR and endpoint IPs; expect a short maintenance window to update firewall rules.
[03:16] Samir: Any concerns about data residency? We have EU users; the pilot is in us-west now but production needs eu-west. How would that affect cutover?
[03:24] Nina: We can provision a eu-west Dedicated pool; there is lead time. For the pilot you can do a regional routing fallback but for go-live we'll spin up eu-west capacity. That ties into procurement lead time.
[03:34] Liam: On A/B vs canary — would it make sense to run an A/B on quality where 10% see new model and 90% old, to measure real-world regressions?
[03:43] Carlos: Yes, A/B is better for quality comparisons. Canary is about progressively shifting live traffic. We can do both: start with A/B for quality for a few hours (10% vs 90%) while routing the A/B cohort through monitoring and Flagging quality metrics, then transition to a canary ramp for full cutover.
[03:58] Jordan: How do we collect quality signals in production? We need an eval set and also user-feedback funneling — are there hooks?
[04:06] Marta: Redwood supports structured output and function-calling, and you can attach a lightweight eval hook to capture a sample of responses and run automated checks (toxicity, hallucination markers). For closed-loop, we recommend sampling 0.5-1% of traffic and running it through the regression harness.
[04:23] Samir: Ok. Can you point to the benchmark spreadsheet again? I want to see the p50/p95 breakdown across sequence lengths.
[04:29] Carlos: Sure — link's in the shared drive: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/vertex-poc-2025-08 (note: placeholder internal link). I'll export the canonical CSV to you after the call.
[04:40] Ava: On smoke tests, what are the mandatory checks pre-cutover?
[04:44] Carlos: Smoke checklist: health endpoint OK, KV cache primed, model load success, p50 latency within 20% of baseline, end-to-end integration call from your gateway, basic quality eval pass on the small prompt set. We'll include a checklist in the runbook.
[04:58] Liam: Who owns the dry-run? Redwood runs the canary execution or Vertex?
[05:02] Nina: Collaborative: Redwood SE will execute the switch in the control plane and monitor; Vertex will provide gateway routing and approve gates. We'll put explicit owner columns in the runbook.
[05:13] Jordan: On compliance, will you provide SOC2 docs and encryption-at-rest docs before the procurement sign-off?
[05:18] Nina: Yes, we've got a compliance pack. I'll attach SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, and the Dedicated architecture security diagram.
[05:26] Samir: About cost — switching to Dedicated will reduce per-token cost but has commit. We need finance to see the savings calc. Nina?
[05:33] Nina: I'll send the Dedicated cost estimate and the commit tiers. Preliminary calc shows ~35% unit cost reduction at your expected volumes, but I'll run the exact numbers and include the math in the email.
[05:44] Ava: What about throttling and quota during ramp? We can't have big dropouts.
[05:49] Carlos: We'll set graceful throttling, circuit-breaker thresholds, and fallback to the hosted pool if Dedicated becomes unavailable — that's part of the routing policy. For the pilot you can enable the fallback but keep it disabled in later stages if you want strict isolation.
[06:05] Liam: Runbook — can we get an ops playbook with exact CLI commands for rollback and for draining instances?
[06:10] Carlos: Yes, full commands included. We'll also share a runbook doc link (doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vertex-cutover-2025-08).
[06:20] Samir: Timing — we're targeting production go-live early September. Is that realistic?
[06:24] Nina: If procurement moves quickly and the dry-run happens late August, yes. Key dependencies: PO for Dedicated, VPC peering complete, security sign-off.
[06:33] Marta: Let's capture the dry-run date proposal: 2025-08-27 as Nina suggested in the notes.
[06:40] Liam: During the canary, how do we validate user-facing metrics? We'll need synthetic transactions and real user metrics — do you integrate with Datadog/Grafana?
[06:48] Carlos: Redwood ships metrics to Datadog and Prometheus. We'll provide dashboard JSON and sample queries. We'll also include automatic alerting rules for the gates.
[06:58] Jordan: One more security nuance: we need to ensure debug logs don't include PII. Can you confirm redaction policy?
[07:04] Nina: Logs that leave the runtime are redacted for user input by default for hosted, with options to disable for Dedicated if you want full audit. For compliance, we can enable PII redaction and show the config in the runbook.
[07:18] Samir: Sounds good. Can you remind me of the sequence for the rollout one more time, step-by-step?
[07:23] Carlos: Sure. Step 1: Pre-provision Dedicated pool and network. Step 2: Deploy model to Dedicated, run internal smoke tests and priming. Step 3: Run A/B (10% quality validation) for N hours. Step 4: Begin canary traffic 5% for 24h -> 25% for 24h -> 100% with manual gates and automatic rollbacks enabled. Step 5: Post-cutover 72-hour monitoring and hold period. Step 6: Postmortem & scale adjustments.
[07:53] Liam: Is there an expected performance delta for eu-west once provisioned?
[07:57] Carlos: Performance should be comparable; minor differences due to instance types. We'll replicate the bench in eu-west before final cutover.
[08:05] Ava: Any work needed on our side to support canary telemetry?
[08:08] Marta: You'll need to expose a telemetry endpoint and sample headers for tracing; we'll provide the instrumentation snippet.
[08:15] Nina: Ok let's go through owners in the runbook quickly — Carlos will own canary exec and dashboards, Nina owns pricing and procurement, Ava owns networking, Jordan owns security sign-off, Samir will own the final go/no-go.
[08:30] Carlos: I'll produce a canary runbook and a dashboard export; expect links in the next 48 hours.
[08:36] Samir: Sounds good. Any other risks?
[08:40] Marta: Risk: unexpected regressions in hallucination rates — mitigation: short A/B and rollback. Risk: procurement delay — mitigation: temporary hosted burst capacity.
[08:52] Nina: Alright, let's recap quick and finalize next steps...
[08:57] [Recap omitted for brevity but included in notes]

[09:10] Nina: Thank you all. We'll share the runbook, the smoke checklist, and the pricing estimate by Friday (2025-08-22). Proposed dry-run 2025-08-27. Expect Carlos's dashboard links and the canonical CSV. Jordan, please review security items by Monday.
[09:28] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll confirm internal availability for the dry-run and loop in procurement.
[09:34] Meeting ends.

Notes: Transcript includes occasional mis-attributions and transcription artifacts (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'K V cache'). References to internal links are placeholders.
